_note: Rubric grades (rubric.md), written blind: by label only, before blind-key.json was read. 1 = the item holds, 0 = it does not. Q1's R6 is given for a complete proof of the observation for all five, by certificate as well as by mechanism; success still needs R1 to R3.

292.notes: No code. Restates the observation as 'f is a cube in the group ring' (f = g g(x^2, y^2)); no explicit g, no mechanism. Says it could not run code.

318.notes: Code. Cube roots in the group ring, computed (dense, ~600-725 terms) but not given, except t's. Searched for small cube roots and order-3 dilation symmetry, found none, and concludes the confinement 'does not come from a simple symmetric sub-rule' and that a tidy structural reason is 'likely to be wrong': misleading, since the half-Frobenius mechanism exists.

464.notes: Code. Norm-to-F4 certificate P_f^2 = P_f for all five (machine-confirmed), so a complete proof of the observation, not of a mechanism; says the structural reason is still open. Correctly flags the '1 in 20,000' chance figure as model-dependent (its ensemble gave 1 in 136).

848.notes: Code. The same norm certificate for all five, machine-confirmed, and a clean univariate cube root of t. Calls the confinement 'a verified coincidence, not a structural consequence' while saying it found no reason: wrong, but stated as a gap.

878.notes: Code. Norm certificate for all five (machine-confirmed); rule 90's confinement explained by Dirichlet's formula, the unit criterion, checked at the eligible primes below 400. Sees (1+x)^2(1+y)^2 dividing f2 but calls the cofactor generic (it is f1). Asserts 'I found no structural cause, and I believe there is none beyond Theorem A': wrong. Correctly says the chance model is wrong for the family (counts all 1,023 unions at several m).

995.notes: No code. Restates as 'f is a cube in R_m'; no g, no mechanism. Says it could not run code.

230.notes: Code. All nine as split cofactor times a cube; rule 90 by the unit criterion, rule 150 by 3 in <4>, so exactly the three at 61; the seven unexplained, with what was excluded. Says it does not believe chance for all seven (against the card's 0.62).

602.notes: Code. All nine; the unit criterion for rule 90; 3 in <4> for the three at 61. Claims rule 4850 has every eigenvalue a ninth power at 37, which would rule out chance for it: to be checked by machine (not a rubric item).

703.notes: Code. All nine, with non-symmetric cube roots g1, g2, g3 and binomial or Phi_3 cofactors; a norm certificate for x + 1 at 37; Phi_3 by telescoping for 61. Seven unexplained.

729.notes: No code, no factorisations. Conjectures all 16 factor into rule-90 atoms on the torus (false for seven) and the three at 61 by a subfield after dilation (wrong). Says it could not run code.

875.notes: Code. No unit-times-cube factorisation; instead the minimum-weight cube roots in the group ring (dense; the machine counts three as found under the registered rule, which admits any cube root). Real finds: 17056 is 1112 under the exponent map (a, b) -> (a + b, a - b), and the per-class cube rates at 37 (0.937 on axis and diagonal) and the corrected expectation of about 5.7, as the sixth pilot found. The seven: chance under the corrected model.

998.notes: No code: eight of the nine by hand in u = t(x), v = t(y) (missed 28944), all machine-confirmed; the right reasons at 37 (rule 90) and 61 (rule 150, 3 = 2^k with k even). Conjectures the other eight are also g h^3 (false for seven).
